meta.name: SaleSonic Demonstration Dataset
meta.premise: 6 deals (one per client) with realistic history, contacts, stages, values and close dates so the SaleSonic LLM has rich context to work with.
howToUseThisData: Load the 6 deals into the demo environment with the contacts, stages, values and close dates above.
Attach the meeting notes/correspondence snippets as activity history.
The anecdotes give the LLM concrete "human" context so recommendations become specific rather than generic.
meta.bottomLine: Load these six deals → the three personas immediately look and feel different: Salesman sees concrete next moves on his deals; Manager sees coaching and risk across the team; Director sees forecast health and big-call decisions.

commercialDNA.description: The single source of truth that calibrates every forecast, recommendation, score and report to the business. Entered once by leadership.
commercialDNA.dataSources: CRM, finance system, HR/comp plans, sales playbook, leadership input.

deals.headline: Deal 1 – Coors | Enterprise Stores Rollout | £600K | WON (closed 15 Jun 2025)

history.note: Discovery call. Lisa flagged major stock-out issues across 120 stores.
Workshop – mapped current vs future process. Mark raised integration concerns with legacy POS.
Proposal presented. Sarah pushed hard on ROI and payback < 14 months.
Technical deep-dive. Mark signed off architecture after we agreed on phased API approach.
Commercial negotiation. Sarah asked for 8% discount + extended support. We held at 5% + free year-1 training.
Final board paper approved.
Contract signed.

deals.anecdote: Lisa became our internal champion after the February workshop. She told Ralph 'If we don't fix stock accuracy before peak season, we'll lose another £2m'. That urgency drove the whole deal.
proofPoints: Held at 5% discount + free year-1 training

deals.headline: Deal 2 – Morrison | Contact Centre Modernisation | £350K | LOST (closed 28 Apr 2025)

history.note: Initial meeting – Helen described high agent attrition and poor CSAT.
Demo of new platform. Strong positive reaction from ops team.
Commercial proposal issued.
Procurement entered. Tom Reid insisted on 3-vendor RFP.
We came second on price to a lower-cost competitor.
David decided to go with the cheaper option "to protect margin this year".

deals.anecdote: Helen was our champion until Procurement took control. She later told Andrew 'I still think your solution was better, but the CFO only looked at year-1 cost'.
deals.lossReason: Price – came second to a lower-cost competitor after Procurement forced a 3-vendor RFP.
deals.lossLearning: Procurement took control late. Ensure Economic Buyer stays engaged earlier next time.

deals.headline: Deal 3 – Barclays | Software Upgrade – Core Banking | £500K | Winning (close 15 Oct 2026)

history.note: Discovery – Sophie highlighted regulatory pressure on legacy system.
Architecture workshop with Amir. Positive technical feedback.
Business case presented. Rachel asked for clearer risk reduction narrative.
Security & compliance review passed (Michael Grant supportive).
Commercial terms agreed in principle.
Final internal governance in progress.

deals.anecdote: Sophie told Brian 'If we miss the FCA timeline I'll be the one explaining it to the Board'. That personal risk is driving her sponsorship.
proofPoints: FCA timeline personal risk for Sophie

deals.headline: Deal 4 – Asda Stores | Enterprise Stores Rollout Phase 2 | £250K | Winning (close 30 Nov 2026)

history.note: Phase 1 success referenced. Karen pushing hard for Phase 2 before Black Friday.
Scope workshop completed.
Proposal accepted in principle.
Budget confirmation delayed by internal re-forecast.
Budget now unlocked. Contract red-lines in legal.

deals.anecdote: Karen said 'Phase 1 saved us 14 minutes per stock take. Multiply that by 600 stores and the business case writes itself'.
deals.blocker: Legal red-lines are the only blocker
proofPoints: Phase 1 saved 14 minutes per stock take

deals.headline: Deal 5 – TFL | Contact Centre Platform | £150K | Losing / At Risk (close 20 Dec 2026)

history.note: Strong start – Chris very engaged.
Technical proof-of-concept successful.
Budget freeze announced across TFL.
Deal stalled. James now prioritising cost reduction over transformation.
Competitor offering 20% lower price entered discussions.

deals.anecdote: Chris told Des last week 'I still want your platform, but James has been told to cut 12% from the cost base. I'm losing the argument'.
deals.blocker: Budget freeze, 12% cost-cut mandate, competitor at 20% lower price

deals.headline: Deal 6 – United Utilities | Software Upgrade – Customer Portal | £100K | Early Pipeline (close 30 Jun 2027)

history.note: First meeting – Amy described poor self-service adoption.
Discovery workshop.
High-level proposal sent.
Waiting for internal prioritisation meeting in October.

deals.anecdote: Amy said 'Customers are still ringing us for things they should be able to do online. Every call costs us £6.40'.
deals.blocker: Waiting for internal prioritisation meeting in October

salesman.title: Salesman
salesman.who: Ralph Kelly, Sean Kearney, Des Hunt, Brian Greenbank, Andrew Fleming

salesman.controls: Daily prioritisation, next-best actions, deal progression and forecast accuracy on their own book.

dashboardSummary.title: Summary – How the three dashboards work together
lines: Salesman → Executes the right actions on individual deals today.
Sales Manager → Coaches, unblocks and protects the team forecast today.
Sales Director → Makes the big calls and controls overall business trajectory.
dashboardSummary.principle: All three views stay calibrated to the same Commercial DNA and the same underlying deal data, so everyone is working from one version of the truth.
dashboardSummary.designPrinciple: Each dashboard is designed so the person can actually control business activity that day, not just look at reports.

capabilities.name: Commercial DNA Setup
capabilities.subtitle: Foundation – done once
capabilities.whatItDoes: Creates the single source of truth that calibrates every forecast, recommendation, score and report to your business.
infoNeeded: Annual/quarterly revenue targets
Services / products sold and typical deal sizes
Compensation plans (quotas, accelerators, commission structure)
Chosen sales methodology (MEDDIC, Challenger, SPIN, Sandler or mix)
Ideal Customer Profile, average sales cycle, target margins
Geographic coverage / territories
Historical win rates (overall + by segment / new vs existing)
capabilities.dataSources: CRM, finance system, HR/comp plans, sales playbook, leadership input.
notes: If win rates look unrealistically high → system flags "possible lack of competitive deals or weak pipeline quality".
If geographic coverage is thin in a territory → flags "new territory risk / under-penetration".

capabilities.name: Calibrated Forecasts
capabilities.whatItDoes: Produces pipeline coverage, forecast confidence, revenue gap and momentum – all adjusted to your Commercial DNA.
infoNeeded: Current pipeline (deals, values, stages, close dates, probabilities)
Historical conversion rates by stage
Win rates by segment, product, territory, deal size
Seasonality and target phasing
capabilities.dataSources: CRM opportunity data + historical closed-won/lost + Commercial DNA targets.
notes: High win rates + low competitive losses → "May indicate not enough competitive deals or sandbagging".
Large pipeline stuck at top of funnel → "Early-stage bloat – conversion risk high, coverage overstated".

capabilities.name: Methodology-Scored Deal Inspections
capabilities.subtitle: MEDDIC scorecard etc.
capabilities.whatItDoes: Scores every live deal against the chosen methodology and highlights gaps.
infoNeeded: Deal contacts (Economic Buyer, Technical Buyer, User Buyer, Champion, Influencer, Approver)
Meeting notes, emails, call summaries
Competitive situation, decision process, metrics, pain, budget, timeline
Current stage and next steps
capabilities.dataSources: CRM contacts & activities, uploaded documents, email/calendar integration, manual notes.
notes: Missing Economic Buyer or weak Champion is immediately flagged.
Stuck deals at top of funnel show low scores on Metrics / Decision Criteria / Paper Process.

capabilities.name: RFP Analyser – Go/No-Go Verdicts
capabilities.whatItDoes: Reads an RFP and gives a clear Go / No-Go recommendation with rationale.
infoNeeded: Full RFP document (PDF, DOCX, TXT)
Your capabilities, win themes, commercial constraints (from Commercial DNA)
Historical win rates on similar RFPs
capabilities.dataSources: Uploaded RFP + Commercial DNA + past RFP outcomes in CRM.

capabilities.name: Document Extract & Analysis
capabilities.whatItDoes: Pulls key commercial intelligence from proposals, contracts, meeting notes, board papers, etc.
infoNeeded: Any PDF / DOCX / TXT document related to a deal or opportunity.
capabilities.dataSources: User upload or linked document store.

capabilities.name: War Room
capabilities.subtitle: 6 Advisory Personas → one logged recommendation
capabilities.whatItDoes: Pressure-tests a major deal or decision with six different advisory lenses and produces a single, logged recommendation.
infoNeeded: Full deal history, contacts, competitive notes, commercial terms, risk factors, methodology scores.
capabilities.dataSources: Everything already in the deal record + Commercial DNA.
notes: Especially powerful when win rates are high (to stress-test whether the deal is truly competitive) or when pipeline is stuck (to decide accelerate vs de-commit).

capabilities.name: Board-Ready Reports & Decision Log
capabilities.whatItDoes: Generates executive narratives and permanently logs every major commercial decision.
infoNeeded: Forecast data, deal inspections, War Room outcomes, targets, momentum trends.
capabilities.dataSources: All of the above + Decision Log entries.

capabilities.name: Forecast & Analysis Planner (9 frameworks) + Strategy Engine
capabilities.whatItDoes: Scenario planning, what-if analysis, milestone & campaign planning.
infoNeeded: Targets, current pipeline, historical conversion, geographic coverage, new territory plans, product mix.
capabilities.dataSources: CRM + Commercial DNA + manual planning inputs.
notes: Highlights "new territory" risk if coverage or historical win rates in that geography are low.
Flags "too much pipeline not moving" when stage velocity is poor.

capabilities.name: Role-Optimised Dashboards & Today's Priorities
capabilities.whatItDoes: Salesman / Manager / Director each see different views with concrete daily actions.
infoNeeded: All deal and activity data above, plus user role and territory assignment.

capabilities.name: Executive Actions (one-click)
capabilities.whatItDoes: 15+ pre-built actions (e.g. "Inspect this deal", "Run War Room", "Generate board paper", "Update forecast confidence").
infoNeeded: Whatever the specific action requires (usually already in the system).

diagnosticSignals.meaning: Not enough competitive deals, weak qualification, or sandbagging
diagnosticSignals.trigger: Closed-won vs closed-lost ratio, competitive mention rate

diagnosticSignals.signal: Large pipeline stuck at top of funnel
diagnosticSignals.meaning: Poor qualification or slow early-stage progression
diagnosticSignals.trigger: Stage age + conversion rates by stage

diagnosticSignals.meaning: Under-penetrated territory or new market risk
diagnosticSignals.trigger: Deals/wins by region vs target coverage

diagnosticSignals.meaning: Learning curve or wrong ICP for that area
diagnosticSignals.trigger: Win rate filtered by geography + deal age

diagnosticSignals.signal: High pipeline coverage but low confidence
diagnosticSignals.trigger: Coverage ratio vs MEDDIC / methodology scores

diagnosticSignals.signal: Deals with missing EB or Champion

diagnosticSignalsShortForm: Win rates unusually high → possible lack of competitive deals or weak qualification
Large volume of pipeline stuck at top of funnel → early-stage bloat / poor conversion
Thin geographic coverage → under-penetrated or new territory risk
New territory low win rate → learning curve or ICP mismatch
High coverage but low confidence → quantity without quality
Missing Economic Buyer or Champion → late-stage collapse risk
dataSourceSummary: CRM (opportunities, contacts, stages, activities, closed history)
Email / calendar (optional integration for richer history)
User activity inside SaleSonic (decision log, War Room outcomes)

minimumViableData.title: Minimum Viable Data to make demos powerful
items: 6–10 live + historical deals with contacts, values, stages and 6–9 months of activity notes
Basic win/loss history (even if only 12 months)
minimumViableData.outcome: Once this data is loaded, the three personas (Salesman, Manager, Director) immediately produce concrete, non-academic recommendations and prioritised daily actions.
